result:
Reasonable as a bounded probe, with one structural flaw: as written it cannot separate "no effect" from "not applied", and both pass channels can be moved by confounds it does not log.

**1. Readback trap.** Self-collision true is normally the articulation API attribute, so the API is applied and a USD `Get()` on the un-authored count attributes returns the installed schema fallback. The omni.physx parser reads that same value, so an applied 32/1 is plausible, but nothing in Python reads the live PhysX articulation object. Your before and after reads only confirm authorship. Concretely:
- Author the counts before the physics scene and warmup exist. A live edit under the GPU tensor pipeline is not guaranteed to reach the existing articulation.
- Prove application by behavior on the same 1-robot source. One repeat of the un-authored run gives the noise floor. Then author velocity iterations 255 for a short run. If the trajectory stays inside that floor, velocity iterations are inert for articulations in this TGS build and the hypothesis is dead before any grid run. Only then does 32/4 mean anything.
- If the pre-physics abort fires on a None read, the API is not applied. Applying it also switches sleep and stabilization thresholds from parser defaults to schema fallbacks. Record HasAPI.

**2. Interpretive trap.** The origin robot already passes at un-authored settings, so "32 only if 1 passes" discriminates nothing. The only 1-robot observable that tests the hypothesis is the proven LM/RM tibia bias: SDK mean near −0.023 rad/s integrating to −0.367 rad against a q-range of 4e-5 rad. Pre-declare it as the outcome. Unchanged within noise means velocity iterations do not govern the SDK velocity channel and the grid run tests something else. Collapsed means every prior RMS verdict, including the origin pass, went through a contaminated channel and must be re-established with thresholds unchanged. Also:
- Grid failures are non-integrating too. 10 rad/s RMS inside 0.0067 rad is not motion. It may be chatter rather than DC bias, so log the per-joint integral mismatch beside RMS.
- Kd acts on that SDK velocity. On the tibia, 0.1055 × 10 rad/s gives about 1.05 Nm, matching your 1.16 Nm peak. So 32/4 changes the plant input on exactly the failing robots. A grid pass cannot be attributed to accuracy rather than to removal of a torque-injection loop.

**3. Confounds.** Hypothesis, checkable on archived data: sleep threshold and wake counter are un-authored, and quiet standing is the state that sleeps. A sleeping row reports zero joint velocity and zero contact impulse. If the next torque write wakes it, you get single-row dropouts, matching 1..10 missing-toe samples on 21 robots with no position dependence. Velocity iterations alter the post-solve velocity that feeds the sleep test, so 32/4 can shift sleep either way. Search archived rows for all six toes at exactly 0 N with all 18 SDK velocities exactly 0.0, and log per-articulation sleep state every row in the new runs. Separately, on a GPU pipeline 11/32 is one draw of unknown variance. Compare per slot, check whether the origin slot inside the grid passed, since a solo pass with an in-grid failure points at batching rather than position, and budget one un-authored grid repeat as control before crediting any count change.
